stem: A minor may not have the right to institute an action for annulment if he actively misrepresented as to his age under the principle of:
explanation: Mercado v. Espiritu: minors who pretend to be of legal age when they sell real property, and thereby induce the other party to contract, are estopped from later seeking to annul the contract on the ground of minority. Minority is a restriction on capacity to act (Art. 38) and ordinarily makes a contract voidable (Art. 1390). Active misrepresentation of age, however, bars the minor from invoking it. Mere silence or a passive statement would not produce estoppel (cf. Braganza v. Villa Abrille).

statements: 1. The personality of corporations, institutions and entities for public interest or purpose, created by law, begins as soon as they have been constituted according to law.
2. Partnerships and associations for private interest or purpose are governed by the laws creating or recognizing them.
choices: No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE, being Art. 44(2). No. 2 is FALSE. Under Art. 45, only the juridical persons in Nos. 1 and 2 of Art. 44 (the State and its political subdivisions, and public-interest entities created by law) are governed by the laws creating or recognizing them. Private corporations are regulated by laws of general application on the subject (now the Revised Corporation Code), and 'partnerships and associations for private interest or purpose are governed by the provisions of this Code concerning partnerships.'

statements: 1. Juridical persons may acquire and possess property of all kinds, as well as incur obligations and bring civil actions; but they may not bring criminal actions.

2. Upon the dissolution of corporations, institutions and other entities for public interest or purpose created by law, if nothing has been specified by law or charter on the disposition of their assets, the property and other assets shall be applied to similar purposes for the benefit of the region, province, city or municipality which during the existence of the institution derived the principal benefits from the same.
choices: No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Art. 46 provides that juridical persons may acquire and possess property of all kinds, incur obligations, and 'bring civil OR CRIMINAL actions, in conformity with the laws and regulations of their organization.' No. 2 is TRUE, being the rule of Art. 47 for the dissolution of public-interest entities under Art. 44(2) when neither the law nor the charter provides for disposition of the assets.

stem: Naturalization and the loss and reacquisition of citizenship of the Philippines are governed by the Civil Code.
explanation: Art. 49: 'Naturalization and the loss and reacquisition of citizenship of the Philippines are governed by SPECIAL LAWS.' These include C.A. 473 (Revised Naturalization Law), R.A. 9139 (Administrative Naturalization Law of 2000), C.A. 63 (loss and reacquisition), and R.A. 9225 (Citizenship Retention and Re-acquisition Act of 2003). The enumeration of citizens in Art. 48 has been superseded by Art. IV of the 1987 Constitution.

statements: 1. For the exercise of civil rights and the fulfillment of civil obligations, the domicile of natural persons is the place of their actual residence.

2. When the law creating or recognizing them, or any other provision does not fix the domicile of juridical persons, the same shall be understood to be the place where their legal representation is established or where they exercise their principal functions.
choices: No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Art. 50 fixes the domicile of natural persons at the place of their HABITUAL residence, not mere actual residence. Domicile requires physical presence plus the intention to remain (animus manendi), while residence may be temporary. No. 2 is TRUE, being the text of Art. 51 on the domicile of juridical persons.

statements: 1. The husband shall fix the family domicile; in case of disagreement between the spouses, the decision of the husband shall prevail.

2. The court may exempt one spouse from living with the other if the latter should live abroad or there are other valid and compelling reasons for the exemption; however, such exemption shall not apply if the same is not compatible with the solidarity of the family.
choices: No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. FC Art. 69 provides that 'the husband and wife shall fix the family domicile. In case of disagreement, the COURT shall decide.' Under the old Civil Code (Art. 110), the husband fixed the residence. The Family Code made it a joint decision of the spouses, consistent with their equality. No. 2 is TRUE, being the second paragraph of FC Art. 69.

stem: To effect a change of domicile, the following must concur, except:
choices: An actual removal or an actual change of domicile
A bona fide intention of abandoning the former place of residence and establishing a new one
Definite acts which correspond with the purpose
Continuous physical presence in the new place for at least one year
explanation: Romualdez-Marcos v. COMELEC (1995): to change domicile, there must be (1) an actual removal or actual change of domicile; (2) a bona fide intention of abandoning the former place of residence and establishing a new one; and (3) definite acts which correspond with the purpose. Without these, the domicile of origin continues. Domicile, once acquired, is retained until a new one is gained, and absence alone does not cause its loss. The Court also held that a wife does not automatically lose her domicile of origin by marriage. No minimum period of physical presence is an element of a change of domicile; the one-year residence requirement for congressional candidates is a separate constitutional qualification.

statements: 1. Under R.A. 6809, emancipation takes place by the attainment of majority, and unless otherwise provided, majority commences at the age of eighteen years.

2. Upon the effectivity of R.A. 6809, existing wills, bequests, donations, grants, insurance policies and similar instruments containing references and provisions favorable to minors shall retroact to their prejudice.
choices: No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE. R.A. 6809 (approved Dec. 13, 1989), Sec. 1, amended FC Art. 234 to lower the age of majority from 21 to 18. Emancipation terminates parental authority, and the child becomes qualified and responsible for all acts of civil life, save exceptions in special laws (FC Art. 236). One such exception: parental consent to marry is still required until age 21 (FC Art. 14). No. 2 is FALSE. Sec. 4 of R.A. 6809 provides that existing wills, bequests, donations, grants, insurance policies and similar instruments containing references and provisions favorable to minors 'will NOT retroact to their prejudice.'

stem: The complete publication of the Family Code was made on August 4, 1987. On September 4, 1987, Junior Cruz and Gemma Reyes were married before a municipal mayor. Was the marriage valid?
choices: No, because the Family Code removed the mayor's authority to solemnize marriages
Yes, because the Family Code took effect only on August 3, 1988; at the time, municipal mayors were empowered to solemnize marriages under the Civil Code
No, because the Family Code took effect 15 days after publication
Yes, because mayors have always been authorized under the Family Code
explanation: Yes. FC Art. 257 provides that the Code 'shall take effect one year after the completion of its publication in a newspaper of general circulation.' Publication was completed on August 4, 1987, so the Family Code took effect on August 3, 1988, 1988 being a leap year. On September 4, 1987, the Civil Code of 1950 still governed, and it authorized municipal mayors to solemnize marriages. (Under the Family Code, mayors were later authorized by the Local Government Code of 1991.)
key_note: The August 3, 1988 effectivity date follows the 365-day count. Under the calendar-year reading (Admin. Code Sec. 31; CIR v. Primetown) it would be August 4, 1988. Either way, the answer is unaffected.
